body.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), the corrected handle \(\mathfrak I\) admits a measurable uniformly bounded right inverse on every observed-data DQM score: if \(s\in L^2_0(P)\) is the score of an observed path through \(P\), there are factorwise centered scores \(s_X,s_\pi,s_Y,s_A,s_Z\) such that
\[
s=E_P\{s_X(X)+s_\pi(J,X)+s_Y(Y,J,X)+s_A(A,J,X)+s_Z(Z,J,X)\mid O\},
\]
and the sum of their factor \(L^2\)-norms is at most \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\|s\|_{L^2(P)}\).  The recovery is measurable in \(X\), uses the augmented finite-feature inverse to fix the differentiated factorization, then uses the conditional \(G(X)^+\) solve for the measurement scores and the pointwise \(\{R^{\mathsf T}DR\}^{-1}\) solve for the remaining mixture and class-density scores.  Class-density scores are support preserving.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(s\) be the score of an observed DQM path and put \(s_X=E_P(s\mid X)\) and \(s_c=s-s_X\).  Conditional DQM differentiation gives a conditional cell-density derivative \(\dot p_r(y\mid x)=p_r(y\mid x)s_c(y,r,x)\), where \(r=(a,z)\).  The augmented finite moments are bounded functions of \(O\); hence their derivatives are conditional expectations of those functions times \(s_c\).  Conditional Jensen's inequality and Lemma 2A give measurable derivatives of \(\pi,M_A,M_Z,\Gamma_Y\) with conditional squared norm bounded by \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}^2E(s_c^2\mid X)\).  This also fixes the locally constant modal labeling.

Differentiate the product factorization.  On supported atoms its formal conditional-score identity is
\[
s_c(y,a,z,x)=\sum_{j=1}^KR_{(a,z),j}(y,x)
 \{s_{\pi,j}(x)+s_{Y,j}(y,x)+s_{A,aj}(x)+s_{Z,zj}(x)\}. \tag{10}
\]
At a zero factor atom a two-sided probability derivative is zero, so the corresponding score may be set to zero.  Although the initially differentiated measurement scores need not yet have a useful uniform norm, (10) is an algebraic identity.

Let \(u\in\mathbb R^{2K^2}\) collect the \(s_A\) and \(s_Z\) coordinates.  Terms in (10) depending only on \((Y,J,X)\) have cell vector in \(\operatorname{range}(R)=\ker(N_B)\).  The measurement term is \(c^{\mathsf T}u\).  Therefore
\[
N_Bs_c=h^{\mathsf T}u. \tag{11}
\]
Taking conditional inner products with \(h\) gives
\[
b_s(X):=E\{hN_Bs_c\mid X\}=G(X)u. \tag{12}
\]
On the \(2K(K-1)\)-dimensional subspace on which every \(A\)- and \(Z\)-block is factorwise centered, the map \(u\mapsto h^{\mathsf T}u\) is injective.  Indeed, if it vanished, then \(c^{\mathsf T}u\in\operatorname{range}R\); subtracting that \(R\)-term would give a zero observed derivative with a nonzero normalized measurement derivative, contradicting the injectivity calculation of Lemma 2A after taking the finite feature moments.  Hence \(\operatorname{rank}G=2K(K-1)\); its remaining \(2K\) null directions are precisely the blockwise constants used below.

Every vector in \(\ker G(X)\) has zero inner product with \(h\) conditionally, so \(b_s(X)\in\operatorname{range}G(X)\).  Choose \(u_0=G^+b_s\).  The nonzero-spectrum gap yields
\[
\|u_0(X)\|_2^2\leq\varepsilon^{-1}E\{(N_Bs_c)^2\mid X\}. \tag{13}
\]
Subtracting from each \(A\)-block its \(M_A(\cdot\mid j,X)\)-mean, and analogously for \(Z\), centers \(u_0\).  Such blockwise constants are annihilated by \(N_Bc\), because their cell image is a linear combination of the columns of \(R\).  Thus centering preserves (11), and, since all weights are at most one and \(K\) is fixed, changes the right side of (13) by at most a constant depending on \(K\).  Call the centered coordinates \(s_A,s_Z\).

Set \(s_0=s_c-c^{\mathsf T}u\).  Equation (11) gives \(N_Bs_0=0\).  Lemma 3A gives \(\ker N_B=\operatorname{range}R\), so, pointwise,
\[
t(y,x)=\{R^{\mathsf T}DR\}^{-1}R^{\mathsf T}Ds_0(y,\cdot,x),
\qquad s_0=Rt. \tag{14}
\]
The posterior Gram gap and the identity \(s_0=Rt\) imply
\[
\int g(y\mid x)\sum_jw_j(y,x)t_j(y,x)^2d\nu(y)
 \leq\varepsilon^{-1}E(s_0^2\mid X=x). \tag{15}
\]
Define
\[
s_{\pi,j}(x)=\int f_j(y\mid x)t_j(y,x)d\nu(y),
\qquad s_{Y,j}(y,x)=t_j(y,x)-s_{\pi,j}(x). \tag{16}
\]
Then \(E(s_Y\mid J,X)=0\).  The measurement scores are factorwise centered, and \(E(s_c\mid X)=0\), so (14) also gives \(\sum_j\pi_js_{\pi,j}=0\).  Thus all scores in (10) have the required conditional centering.  Equations (10)--(16) give the requested right inverse.  Bounds (13)--(15), the uniform Euclidean bound on \(N_B\) from cell positivity, and conditional Jensen give the asserted global \(L^2\) bound.

All displayed inverses and pseudoinverses are Borel measurable on their fixed-rank strata.  Finally, common support gives \(f_j>0\) \(\nu\)-almost everywhere.  Equation (16) is a class-density score with \(\int f_js_{Y,j}d\nu=0\); the bounded truncations \(s_{Y,j}^{(M)}\), recentered under \(f_j\), generate positive normalized exponential-tilt paths and converge in class-factor \(L^2\).  This proves support-preserving recovery and completes the handle.
